top_signals.title: China’s Military Expansion in Southeast Asia Masks a More Complicated Reality
top_signals.summary:
The Chinese Ministry of Defense’s announcement of a “joint support and training center” at an airport in Ban Keun, Laos, on Sept. 29 drew attention to the People’s Liberation Army’s growing footprint in Southeast Asia. Although China does not call it a “base” and said it’s “not targeted at any third party,” it is China’s first publicly acknowledged overseas military facility centered on airpower. Ban Keun joins Djibouti and Cambodia’s Ream Naval Base as nodes in a burgeoning network of overseas Chinese security infrastructure.Concern is understandable. While smaller than China’s base in Djibouti, satellite imagery reveals eight light attack aircraft
